newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends lower on poor leads.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends lower on poor leads.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices ended lower in quiet trading as players were mostly sidelined amid uncertainty in the Tokyo market, dealers said.
"The market was easier. Poor leads and lack of strong buying interest continued to drag down local prices," a dealer said, adding that only South Koreans interest was seen for SMR grades.
But dealers said prices are not really attractive and buyers turned to the sidelines.
The market continues to wait for the return of the Europeans after the summer holidays. Trading was sluggish with activity mainly from hand-to-mouth basis.
Dealers said there was an ample supply of stock in the market and overseas consumers continuing to wait at the sidelines on speculation of lower levels.
Dealers said SMR CV was offered at 372-375 cents, SMR L at 352-354, SMR 5 at 322-325, SMR 10 at 311-313, SMR 20 at 310-312 and drum latex at 243-245.
At the close, October RSS 1 buyer fell 1.50 cents to 320 cents ($1.28) a kg and October SMR 20 buyer was down a cent at 310.50.
